'''János Dezső Aczél''' {{Post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} ({{IPA|hu|ˈɒt͡seːl|lang}}; 26 December 1924 – 1 January 2020),<ref name="mta"/><ref>[https://uwaterloo.ca/pure-mathematics/news/we-remember-distinguished-professor-emeritus-janos-aczel We remember Distinguished Professor Emeritus János Aczel], University of Waterloo</ref> also known as '''John Aczel''',<ref>{{cite news|title=Obituary. John Aczel|newspaper=Ottawa Citizen|date=January 11, 2020|url=https://ottawacitizen.remembering.ca/obituary/john-aczel-1078242125}}</ref> was a [[Hungarian people|Hungarian]]-[[Canadians|Canadian]] mathematician, who specialized in [[functional equations]] and [[information theory]].

==Professional career==
Aczél earned a doctorate in mathematical analysis from the [[University of Budapest]], and held positions at the [[University of Cologne]], [[University of Debrecen|Kossuth University]], [[University of Miskolc]], and [[University of Szeged]].<ref name="ucla">[http://personal.anderson.ucla.edu/marschak.colloquium/1998-99/abstracts/29jan99.htm Biography as a speaker at the Marschak Colloquium at UCLA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031023143306/http://personal.anderson.ucla.edu/marschak.colloquium/1998-99/abstracts/29jan99.htm |date=23 October 2003 }}, 1999, accessed 25 January 2013.</ref>  He joined the [[University of Waterloo]] faculty in 1965, eventually becoming Distinguished Professor in the Department of Pure Mathematics.<ref>[https://math.uwaterloo.ca/pure-mathematics/officers-and-administration/emeritusadjunct Emeritus/Adjunct faculty], Pure Mathematics, Waterloo, accessed 25 January 2013.</ref>

He was the founder of the journal ''[[Aequationes Mathematicae]]'', first published in 1968, and remained its honorary editor-in-chief.<ref>[https://www.springer.com/birkhauser/mathematics/journal/10?detailsPage=editorialBoard Editorial board of ''Aequationes Mathematicae''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080614044138/https://www.springer.com/birkhauser/mathematics/journal/10?detailsPage=editorialBoard |date=14 June 2008 }}, accessed 25 January 2013.</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Aczél held honorary degrees from the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology|University of Karlsruhe]], the [[University of Graz]], and the [[University of Silesia|University of Silesia in Katowice]].<ref name="ucla"/>
In 1971, he was elected a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]].<ref>[http://rsc-src.ca/en/search-fellows RSC Fellow listing] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200204103715/https://rsc-src.ca/en/search-fellows |date=4 February 2020 }}, accessed 25 January 2013.</ref> He was the 1988 winner of the [[Santiago Ramón y Cajal]] Medal.<ref name="ucla"/> In 1990, he became an external member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]],<ref name="mta">[http://mta.hu/oldmta_en/?pid=859&LANG=e&TID=0 Member listing], [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]], accessed 25 January 2013.</ref> and, in 2004, he was honored by the academy as one of the "big five" - five distinguished Hungarian mathematicians born in 1924 and graduating/obtaining a doctorate in 1947. The other honorees were [[John Horvath (mathematician)|John Horvath]], [[Steven Gaal]], [[Ákos Császár]] and [[László Fuchs]].<ref name=big5>{{cite web|url=https://mta.hu/english/big-five-100-video-of-the-international-conference-celebrating-the-100th-anniversary-of-the-birth-of-five-legendary-mathematicians-113767|title=Big Five 100 – Video of the international conference celebrating the 100th anniversary of the birth of five legendary mathematicians|publisher=Hungarian Academy of Sciences|access-date=2025-07-05}}</ref> In 2008, he became an honorary member of the [[Hamburg Mathematical Society]], the oldest active mathematical society in the world.<ref>[http://mta.hu/news_and_views/janos-aczels-latest-honour-68421/ János Aczél's Latest Honour], [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]], accessed 25 January 2013.</ref>

In 2004, he won the Kampé de Fériet Award of the annual Information Processing and Management of Uncertainty conference, "for his pioneering work on the theory of functional equations, with applications in many fields, such as information measures, index numbers, group decision making, aggregation, production functions, laws of science, theory of measurement and utility theory."<ref>[http://ipmu.lip6.fr/?KampeDeFerietAward Kampé de Fériet Award], IPMU, accessed 25 January 2013.</ref>

Issues of the journal ''Aequationes Mathematicae'' were dedicated to Aczél in 1999, 2005, and 2010, in honor of his 75th, 80th, and 85th birthdays. He died at the age of 95 on 1 January 2020.<ref name="luce">{{citation|title=Personal reflections on an unintentional behavioral scientist|first=R. Duncan|last=Luce|authorlink=R. Duncan Luce|journal=Aequationes Mathematicae|volume=58|issue=1–2|pages=3–15|doi=10.1007/s000100050088|year=1999|s2cid=14749650 }}.</ref><ref>{{citation
